findings.text: 适合需要调查有权检查的 Electron 发布包、缺少原始工程，并将线索交给同事复核的工程师。一次任务可先定位一个预加载边界，再交付原件身份、可复核位置与覆盖缺口。
DSH 通过原生 MCP 客户端以 stdio 启动独立 REA 工具。服务端按工具契约绑定分析回调，代表性 JavaScript 静态路径对目录或 ASAR 建立清单并生成带来源和限制的证据。
检查 REA 根发布清单、DSH 专用 setup 与退出路径、MCP 入口及代表性的 JavaScript/Electron 目录和 ASAR 静态链。其他格式、动态和原生分析后端留在范围外。未查 npm 安装成品、未执行目标代码或 DSH。
清单声明 rea-agents 6.9.0，以脚本为 CLI 入口并列 dist。DSH 使用 setup 生成组合配置。没有核实 npm 内容、包版本与提交对应关系或真实宿主兼容。

#### 成本

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 首次使用 | Node、构建产物与存储资源，具体支出未知 | 固定环境、审查 home 改动、准备对照样本 | 包成品与目标 DSH 组合待验 |
| 持续使用 | 静态分析耗用与模型请求费用未知 | 记录输入范围、报告复核与行为对照 | 以每份合格报告为计量单位 |
| 失败恢复 | 重算与额外请求成本未知 | 排查启动、读取部分结果、恢复配置 | 部分解析或回读冲突需分支核查 |
| 退出 | 样本与证据归档资源未知 | 恢复独立 home 或只移除预期登记并复查 | 共享 home 上的装载与清理未实测 |
[Q04](#research-q04) 有兼容环境和已知自有样本时，可在隔离 home 试用。确认只修改预期的 Cordis 文件，再核对同一次宿主握手、工具发现和一条可回源结果。若启动或证据核查失败，关闭隔离实例并转终端或手工解包。共享 home 用卸载动作前需要核对会扫描的客户端与保留回执。

#### 效果

| 效果项 | 当前证据支持 | 尚不能确定 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 接入和配置核对 | DSH 方言的登记发布、冲突处理与重读验证 | 对应 npm 产物与实际宿主能否握手 |
| 静态调查 | 图项表示文件、哈希和解析覆盖，证据携带原件身份 | 动态路径真值、不同打包条件的定位率 |
| 同事复核 | 证据提供统一的输入标识和范围说明 | 对照手工解包的总时间和错判变化 |
[Q02](#research-q02) 配置发布回读包括期望登记与其他服务器的原值，遇竞争而退出可避免继续猜测文件状态。[Q03](#research-q03) 静态分析同时保存输入哈希、文件级覆盖和错误原因，适合用来重放有限主张。
[Q03](#research-q03) 将根哈希、图项来源、查询参数与解析缺口放在同一份证据中，让接手人定位结论适用的包和范围。[Q02](#research-q02) 通过原生 MCP 组合复用已有 DSH 会话，支持将分析和后续追问放在一处。
[Q02](#research-q02) 本地配置回读与宿主启动是两道边界。[Q03](#research-q03) 静态图里的候选边仍需结合原件和可观察行为验证，部分解析尤其容易让遗漏变成错误的否定结论。
[Q05](#research-q05) 可在证据输出之上要求报告逐条填写原件、位置和未覆盖范围，再检查一项可观察行为。这个设计是否少一次误修并缩短复核时间，要与自由汇报做同预算盲评。

#### 启动与依赖

| 依赖或条件 | 是否必需 | 用途 | 缺失或不满足时 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Node ^22.23.4、^24.22.1 或 >=26.12.1 和 REA 构建成品 | 必需 | 启动 CLI 与 MCP | 版本检查或运行产物检查会报错 |
| 支持 Cordis 家目录补丁和原生 MCP 客户端的 DSH | DSH 接入必需 | 读取 Cordis 登记并以 stdio 启动 REA | 配置可能写入但工具无法发现 |
| 已授权且可读取的 Electron 目录或 ASAR | 代表任务必需 | 固定输入并生成静态图 | 无法读取或部分解析时相应结论范围会缩小 |
| procps 兼容的 ps | Linux 静态任务依作者说明需具备 | 检查分析进程归属 | 按环境补齐后再检查，或使用另一种手工路径 |
| Hopper、Ghidra、IDA 等 | 各原生后端按需 | 对应原生逆向任务 | 本次 Electron 代表链无需引入这些后端 |

technical.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) DSH 的 stdio 接入是复用宿主能力的局部适配，原创档只计有实际 DSH 配置回读的增量。[Q03](#research-q03) 文件级范围和根身份绑定改善调查证据的可追溯性，机制按实质增量计，动态真值不随之成立。相同目录或 ASAR 调查链可迁移到 CLI 与其他 MCP 客户端，仍需各自适配。把资产、覆盖和图合入统一证据减少人工拼接，按实质组合计，完整调查仍需人工对照。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 手工提取、分析与交接之间增加清楚的证据交付责任，流程取实质增量。[Q03](#research-q03) 统一的哈希、范围和图项使验收人可核对同一版产物，交付取实质增量。缺少原始工程但已有 DSH 的人可以直接尝试工具，同类终端途径也存在，触达仅小幅。[Q04](#research-q04) 结构化证据可能省交接整理，范围复核和兼容成本仍由用户承担，成本结构只计小幅增量。

recommendation.reason: 已有兼容 DSH 与 Node 的工程师可以用 REA 调查一份有权检查的 Electron 构建物。相比手工解包并另记笔记，REA 将产物哈希、图项和覆盖限制合成可复查的证据。如果宿主未发现工具或关键线索无法回到包内位置，请停止试用并改用终端或手工解包核对。

scenario.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) README 63–67、119–128 和证据对象明确了面向无源码构建物的重复调查与可交接结果，比偶发便利有更明确目标。没有用户工作量和错误记录，无法确认这种摩擦的频率和后果足以达到较充分档。

advantage.rationale: [Q03](#research-q03) JavaScriptApplicationEvidence.ts 67–86 将根哈希、参数及限制结构化，图项又带覆盖状态，超出单纯入口包装。相比已有 REA CLI，DSH 主要增加会话内调用。同一任务的静态归因正确率与人工复核收益未知，取部分成立而非较充分。

evidence.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) SetupClientConfiguration.ts 444–513 与 launcher 61–84 追到发布失败、回读与实际服务；[Q03](#research-q03) 服务回调追到产物证据与解析缺口，支持有条件试用并超出声明级材料。没有同版宿主或本地执行结果，到此为源码级上限。

cost.rationale: [Q04](#research-q04) 清单列出 Node 区间，Uninstall.ts 1231–1255、1324–1339 有保留和成功回执，独立 home 给出可恢复的有限试用路径，高于退出缺口大的低档。配置核对、工具发现和静态结果回查须人工承担，未测真实清理及总投入，取部分成立。

publication.summaries.text: 通过终端或 MCP 调查原生二进制、JavaScript、Electron、.NET 与网站，输出分析证据及限制。

items.模型工具: 通过 DSH 原生 MCP 客户端使用 REA 应用静态调查，在证据中保存原件与范围
items.用户命令: 用 REA CLI 的 setup 生成宿主配置，以 mcp 命令启动标准流服务

publication.capabilities.table:
| 能力 | 主要用途 | 使用条件与边界 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DSH MCP 组合配置 | 挂载独立的 REA 服务 | 确认 home、启动路径和宿主原生 MCP 客户端 |
| Electron 静态分析 | 查找目录或 ASAR 内的模块与脚本入口 | 依赖读取和解析范围，运行行为须独立核对 |
| 可回源证据 | 核对原件身份、选择范围和部分解析 | 根哈希与图表示对应产物，逐条推断需追到位置 |

\n\n---\n\nSee a feature in an app that you want in your own product? Ask your agent to investigate it with REA. It can inspect the app without its source code, explain how the feature works, show the evidence, and build a version for your project.\n\nREA connects your agent to tools for inspecting native binaries, JavaScript and Electron apps, .NET assemblies, and websites. You can also use the same tools from your terminal. Analysis runs locally, and results include the evidence and limitations behind each conclusion.\n\nSetup registers REA with your agent and installs matching workflow instructions. Native analysis can use an existing Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna installation; setup can optionally install Hopper with approval. Static JavaScript analysis needs no native analysis engine.\n\n> **[Visit the REA website](https://rea.tools/)** for setup instructions, illustrated guides, and real case studies.\n\n## Quick start\n\nOn Linux, Ghidra, JADX, firmware tool launches and static JavaScript/Electron\nanalysis require a procps-compatible system `ps` for process ownership\nchecks. Recovery steps are in `docs/getting-started/installation.md` under\n\"Linux owned-process prerequisite\".\n\n### Set up your agent\n\nWith Node.js and npm installed, run:\n\n```bash\nnpx rea-agents setup\n```\n\nChoose your agents, review the proposed changes, and approve them. Setup adds\nREA's MCP server and matching workflow instructions, with backups of existing\nconfiguration. Restart your agent afterward. Setup records the selected runtime and REA\nentry script directly. If acquired through a package runner, keep its cache entry\navailable. Run package acquisition from a trusted directory outside the target\nproject. Installation and recovery details are in the setup guide below.\n\nSetup supports Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and\n[other agents](docs/getting-started/installation.md#supported-agents). See\n[installation and setup](docs/getting-started/installation.md) for provider configuration,\nmanual MCP registration, Claude Code/Codex plugins, and the Cursor Marketplace\nplugin.\n\nMCP advertises compact input schemas to reduce context overhead; guidance a\ncompact schema omits follows the tool description. The full tool set and\ncanonical server validation are unchanged. See \"Compact input schema profile\"\nin the MCP contracts guide.\n\nOutput schemas are omitted from `tools/list` by default: no model API reads\nthem, and REA validates every result itself. Set\n`REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=compact` to advertise each output schema within\na 4,096-byte budget. Both settings keep canonical server-side validation and\ncomplete structured results. See \"Output schemas\" in the MCP contracts guide.\n\n### Ask your agent\n\n```text\nUnderstand how search works in the Notes app, show me the evidence, and build a\nsimilar feature for my project.\n```\n\nReplace Notes with your target app and the feature you want to understand.\n\n### Use the terminal\n\nInspect an extracted JavaScript/Electron app directory or ASAR:\n\n```bash\nnpx -y rea-agents@latest analyze-javascript-application /absolute/path/to/app --json\n```\n\nThe result includes modules, imports, Electron boundaries and their evidence.\nReplace the path with your target, such as `\"D:/apps/example\"` on Windows.\n\nTo install the `rea` command for regular use:\n\n```bash\nnpm install --global rea-agents\nrea --help\n```\n\nFor native analysis, configure a provider first. See the\n[CLI and Evidence guide](docs/getting-started/cli.md) for native commands, provider selection,\nsnapshots and scripting.\n\n### Update REA\n\nREA changes quickly, and new releases include frequent bug fixes. Keep your\ninstallation up to date.\n\nFor a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`:\n\n```bash\nrea update\n```\n\n`rea --update` is an alias for this verified workflow and accepts the same global\noutput flags. Use `rea update` when combining it with other command controls.\n\nUpdater commands retain at most 4 MiB of stdout and stderr combined. Oversized\nmetadata replies are rejected after the command exits; verbose installs continue\nwith bounded diagnostics. Human progress output respects terminal backpressure\nand waits for submitted writes to finish.\n\nBun global updates require Bun 1.2.17 or later. With an older Bun release,\nupgrade Bun manually before running `rea update`.\n\nTo refresh your agent registrations and skill, run the setup command printed\nby the update.\n\nIf you use `npx`, update your agent setup with:\n\n```bash\nnpx rea-agents@latest setup\n```\n\nReview the setup changes and restart your agent. For one-off CLI commands,\nuse `npx rea-agents@latest` followed by the command. With Bun, use\n`bunx rea-agents@latest` in place of `npx rea-agents@latest`.\n\n## How REA works\n\nYour agent calls REA through MCP to inspect the target and trace relevant code.\nREA returns findings with their evidence. The agent uses them to ask follow-up\nquestions, explain the behavior, or write and test an implementation.\nCLI commands use the same workflows.\n\n![REA investigation flow: your agent asks about a local target, REA inspects and traces it using analysis tools, and the agent uses the returned code, references and unknowns to explain, implement and test.](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg)\n\n[Open the full-size figure](website/public/assets/figures/rea-investigation-flow.svg).\n\n\n\n## What you can analyze\n\nREA requires Node.js 22.x (>=22.23.4), 24.x (>=24.22.1), or 26.12.1+, plus npm.\nAdditional tools and host support depend on the target:\n\n| Target | What REA returns | Requirements and guide |\n| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| Desktop installations | Runtime candidates, supporting files, component markers and next probes | Built-in bounded directory/header inspection; The machine that builds it needs Linux on amd64 or arm64, Docker and the agentenv framework version the guide pins.\n\n[Set up desktop app environments](docs/desktop-build-computer.md)\n\n## FAQ\n\n
\nWhich agents can use REA?\n\nAny agent that supports local MCP servers. Setup configures the\n[supported agents](docs/getting-started/installation.md#supported-agents); other clients can use\n[manual MCP registration](docs/getting-started/installation.md#mcp-registry).\n\n
\n\n
\nDo I need a native analysis engine?\n\nDeep native analysis uses Hopper, Ghidra, IDA or Kuna, depending on the target\nand operation. Static JavaScript and .NET inspection work without a native\nanalysis engine. Setup can install Hopper after approval; Ghidra, IDA and Kuna\nuse your existing installations. See [provider setup](docs/getting-started/installation.md#hopper)\nfor the options and their supported targets.\n\n
\n\n
\nDo I need to start Hopper first?\n\nREA starts Hopper when an operation needs it. On macOS, a first-run dialog may\nask you to choose demo mode or activate your license. Complete that prompt in the\nsame user session before your first CLI/MCP operation or unattended job. Open\nHopper manually if needed. See\n[Hopper startup and troubleshooting](docs/getting-started/installation.md#launcher-paths-and-troubleshooting).\n\n
\n\n
\nWhat does installing the skill from skills.sh do?\n\nThe skill supplies investigation instructions for your agent. Use `npx rea-agents setup`\nto register REA's MCP server and install the matching instructions, then restart\nyour agent. See [skill-only installation](docs/getting-started/installation.md#skill-only-installation).\n\n
\n\n
\nWhat code does REA return?\n\nNative analysis returns pseudocode and assembly. JavaScript/Electron analysis\nrecovers modules and their relationships. Your agent uses these findings to\nwrite and test an implementation; the [showcases](#showcases) give worked examples.\n\n
\n\n
\nDoes REA upload my app?\n\nREA analyzes targets locally. Your agent receives the tool results, and its\nmodel provider has its own data policy.\n\n
\n\n
\nWhat should I do if I hit a bug?\n\nUpdate first; a recent release may already fix it.\n\nFor a CLI installed with `npm install --global` or `bun add --global`:\n\n```bash\nrea update\n```\n\nFor agent setup through `npx`:\n\n```bash\nnpx rea-agents@latest setup\n```\n\nIf you're using an agent, complete the [setup refresh](#update-rea) and restart\nit. Retry the same task. If the problem persists, [open an issue](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues)\nwith your REA version, target type, steps to reproduce and error output.\n\n

ProviderBinding : never)\n | (ContractInput extends { readonly detail: \"complete\" | \"summary\" }\n ? RetainedSummaryBinding>\n : never);\n\n/** MCP bindings keyed by their exact contract name. */\nexport type ContractToolBindings = {\n readonly [Name in CatalogToolName]?: Start with [installation and setup](installation.md)\nfor the reviewed setup transaction and [client IDs](installation.md#supported-agents).\nThe versioned verification notes below describe their stated runs; live service\nacceptance is verified only where explicitly recorded.\n\n## Launchers and PATH\n\nA client launched from a desktop app, IDE or service can inherit a different\n`PATH` from your terminal. An absolute path to `rea-agents` does not resolve its\ninterpreter: the npm launcher's `#!/usr/bin/env node` still searches `PATH` for\nNode. Running that command successfully in a terminal does not establish that\nthe client can launch it.\n\nFor JavaScript installations, setup registers the selected runtime\nexecutable and REA script by absolute path. On POSIX, it prefers executable\n`node` or `bun` and REA aliases on setup's `PATH` only when they resolve to the\nsame selected files. This preserves manager-owned aliases across version updates;\notherwise setup uses the selected paths directly. This also applies when setup\nruns through a package runner: retain the selected cache entry and runtime while\nthe registration uses them. Clearing either makes startup fail without resolving\nanother package from the client's project. Restore the same installation before\nrepairing it; an unidentified registration remains untouched. See\n[installation and recovery](installation.md#package-runners-and-global-installation).\nSetup forwards supported, explicitly selected REA settings into client\nconfiguration, but does not copy unrelated ambient environment values. To refresh an older registration, preview\n`rea setup --client --skill=false --dry-run`, then run the same command\nwithout `--dry-run` and approve the displayed changes. Setup preserves unrelated\nsettings, backs up changed configuration and leaves an aligned registration\nunchanged. Restart the client after applying the update.\n\nIf a runtime manager removes the registered executable and no surviving alias\nwas available, doctor reports its identity as unknown and setup retains the\nregistration. REA does not infer that an arbitrary missing executable was Node\nfrom its script argument. Back up the client's configuration, verify the absolute\npath and supported version of the runtime you intend to use, then update only\nthe runtime command, preserving the REA script arguments and other settings.\nRerun setup to review the registration and restart the client.\n\nDoctor JSON records each registration's `command_identity` as `owned`, `foreign`,\nor `unknown`, separately from its readiness `state`. An invalid timeout or client\npolicy can leave ownership established. Setup uses that recorded observation for\nits default client selection, then inspects selected configuration again before\nplanning writes; a missing or unreadable launcher remains unknown.\n\nA retained command does not prove the client selects it. Doctor also checks\nthat client's native transport selectors; a higher-priority remote selector can\nleave the command owned while alignment remains unknown. Metadata that is not a\nnative connection selector is preserved rather than interpreted as a transport.\n\n`rea mcp doctor --json` tests the production MCP adapter using the runtime\nexecutable and environment of the terminal running doctor. It does not launch\nthe client's configured command or reproduce the client's environment. If doctor\npasses but the client disconnects, inspect the client's startup error and registered\nlauncher; see [verification scope](../development/client-verification.md#launch-environment-verification).\n\n`rea doctor` has the same limit for provider checks, and reports a provider setting\nthe registration's file does not carry as a\n[non-blocking unknown](installation.md#check-readiness-for-your-task).\n\n## Setting launch variables in PowerShell\n\nShell examples that prefix a command with `REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=compact`\nuse POSIX shell syntax. In PowerShell, set the process environment before\nlaunching REA:\n\n```powershell\n$env:REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE = \"compact\"\nrea mcp doctor --json\n```\n\nThe assignment applies to the current PowerShell process and commands it launches.\nRestore the previous value when finished, or use\n`Remove-Item Env:REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE` if it was previously unset. It does\nnot update an already running MCP server or desktop client.\n\nTo select this profile for an agent, set `REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE` in that\nclient's existing REA registration `env` object (`environment` for OpenCode) and\nrestart the client, preserving its other settings. A successful terminal doctor run does not verify the client's\nlaunch environment. See [launch-environment verification](../development/client-verification.md#launch-environment-verification)\nand the client-specific instructions below. REA setup forwards supported selections,\nincluding `REA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE`, from its environment into the registration;\nit does not copy unrelated environment values. Restoring the shell's previous\nvalue does not undo a selection already saved by setup.\n\n## Runtime settings and client deadlines\n\n`update_analysis_settings` changes curated defaults inside the running REA\nserver. It does not edit the client registration, extend the client's tool-call\ndeadline, or recompute timeout values previously derived by `rea setup`. When\nraising a REA startup or operation deadline, separately ensure the client allows\nenough time for the full request. Use `inspect_analysis_settings` for the running\nserver's defaults; `rea doctor` checks launch configuration and cannot observe\nanother process's runtime overrides. See the\n[settings design](../design/limits-and-recovery.md) for ownership and lifetime.\n\n## Client tool names and discovery\n\nREA advertises canonical names such as `binary_session`. The MCP host decides\nhow to expose them to its model: a name such as `mcp__rea__binary_session` is a\nclient convention, not a prefix REA can enforce. Use the active client's tool\nlisting and server association to find the operation. A valid registration or\ninstalled skill does not prove that those tools reached the model. Doctor reports\nlive-server identity as unknown; query `binary_session` through the active client\nto observe the running server's identity.\n\nIf a client or fork exposes several servers under the same prefix, a wildcard\nfor that prefix does not isolate REA permissions. Inspect that client's actual\ntool names and approval rules before selecting a permission scope. REA setup\ndoes not repair a client's naming behavior or infer permission drift from an\nunfamiliar prefix. The unavailable fork reported in\n[#5512](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/5512) has not been reverified.\n\n\n\n## Hot/cold catalogs\n\nFor a client that supports MCP catalog refresh, set\n`REA_MCP_TOOL_CATALOG_PROFILE=hot-cold` in REA's server environment and restart\nthe connection. REA then advertises a small initial catalog and loads other\nnamed tools through `discover_tools`. Setup can record the explicit choice:\n\n```bash\nrea setup --client codex --tool-catalog-profile hot-cold --dry-run\nrea setup --client codex --tool-catalog-profile hot-cold\n```\n\nThe plan shows `REA_MCP_TOOL_CATALOG_PROFILE=hot-cold` before approval. This\nselects server catalog loading; enable and verify the client's catalog refresh\nseparately. Setup preserves its existing feature flags and tool approval lists.\nTo restore upfront advertisement, use `--tool-catalog-profile full`, then\nreconnect. Omitting the option preserves the saved profile and keeps `full` for\na new registration. Existing explicit environment selections are also retained.\n\nSetup does not infer refresh from a client name or enable experimental client\nfeatures. The verified Codex trial below covers one version with an explicit\nflag; FastMCP was tested with explicit refresh calls. Neither establishes\nautomatic refresh for every installed version or other client. Keep `full`\nuntil refresh is established for the selected client and configuration.\nSee the [discovery contract](../reference/mcp-contracts.md#hotcold-catalog-discovery) for\npagination, identity and family-scope semantics.\n\nAnalysis tools, including `inspect_analysis_view`, load on demand. For example,\nload `inspect_api_contract` and supply its `view` to answer an initial OpenAPI\nor GraphQL question directly. When later questions need retained facts, load\n`inspect_analysis_view` and use the complete `parent_evidence_id`; source files\nneed not be reopened. If both tools are needed from the start, request both\nnames in one `discover_tools` batch to avoid another catalog refresh. The same\npattern applies to selected Playwright trace and endpoint-comparison results.\nThis defers unused schema delivery and client validator preparation; it does\nnot reduce parsing work, alter Evidence or shorten requested facts. Clients\nwithout catalog refresh should keep the default `full` profile.\n\nCodex CLI 0.165.0 requires its experimental `mcp_tool_list_changed` feature for\nthis workflow. Merge these entries into the existing `~/.codex/config.toml`\nwithout replacing other feature or REA settings:\n\n```toml\n[features]\nmcp_tool_list_changed = true\n\n[mcp_servers.rea.env]\nREA_MCP_TOOL_CATALOG_PROFILE = \"hot-cold\"\n```\n\nThe server setting alone does not enable client refresh. If a successful\ndiscovery call is followed by a missing tool, check the client's refresh feature\nand tool allow/deny lists. Clients without refresh should use the default\n`REA_MCP_TOOL_CATALOG_PROFILE=full`; reconnect after changing it. The\n[FastMCP HTTP trial](#fastmcp-and-unsloth-sse-catalog-limits) below covers\nexplicit refreshes; other clients' automatic refresh remains unverified.\n\n## FastMCP and Unsloth SSE catalog limits\n\nIf an HTTP client reports `Server-sent event exceeded the 1048576 byte limit`\nduring `tools/list`, merge these settings into the **REA server process's**\nenvironment, then reconnect:\n\n```text\nREA_MCP_OUTPUT_SCHEMA_PROFILE=compact\nREA_MCP_TOOL_CATALOG_PROFILE=full\n```\n\nThis advertises all tools without requiring catalog refresh. Compact output\nschemas widen client-side validation; REA still validates complete results\nagainst the canonical contracts. The default output profile, `off`, omits\noutput schemas and is smaller still. See [output schemas](../reference/mcp-contracts.md#output-schemas).\n\nOn main `3e0599a94`, a real FastMCP 4.1.6 / Python MCP 2.3.0 HTTP client with\nthe default 1 MiB SSE event limit rejected the 4,108,975-byte full catalog.\nThe settings above delivered every tool of that catalog in 611,305 bytes and a\n`binary_session` call succeeded. These are measured SSE response sizes for\nthat catalog, not a size guarantee for future catalogs or other profiles.\n\nFor a client that refreshes tools, combine `hot-cold` with the compact schema\nsettings to reduce initial context further: the same trial delivered six\ninitial tools in 33,903 bytes, then explicitly refreshed through 34 loaded\ntools. Hot/cold alone later exceeded the SSE limit during refresh. Follow\nthe [refresh requirements](#hotcold-catalogs).\n\nThe Unsloth report [#9093](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/9093) fails at\ncatalog delivery; the Unsloth application itself was not exercised in this\ntrial. Schema compaction does not bound analysis results. Continue to use\nsummary/detail selection and tool-specific paging for larger results; client\nreceive limits and full Evidence access still apply.\n\n## Fiddler Everywhere alongside REA\n\nConnect Fiddler Everywhere's MCP server separately for HTTP traffic debugging,\npreserving your REA client entry. See the\n[setup instructions and public skills](../guides/web/web-network-captures.md#fiddler-everywhere-mcp-and-public-skills).\n\n## VS Code\n\n`rea setup --client vscode` configures the default VS Code user profile's\n`mcp.json`. Setup honors `VSCODE_PORTABLE` and `VSCODE_APPDATA` when they are\npresent in its environment. It cannot infer a running window's named profile\nor `--user-data-dir`; configure that profile separately when needed.\n\n`rea setup --client copilot_cli` instead configures Copilot's user\n`mcp-config.json`. VS Code can forward eligible profile servers to Copilot\nsessions; see the [VS Code MCP configuration reference](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/reference/mcp-configuration).\n\n## GitHub Copilot CLI\n\nSetup preserves an existing `tools` selection in the REA registration, including\nan empty list. New registrations default to `[\"*\"]`. A restricted selection is\naligned configuration; doctor does not widen it to expose every REA tool. See\n[Copilot's MCP configuration](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/customize-copilot/add-mcp-servers)\nfor tool-selection settings.\n\nFor GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.95, `gpt-4.1` model metadata blocked ordinary\nchat with REA's former full input-schema profile before sending a model request\n(`compaction_static_context_blocked`; [#1554](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/1554)).\nThat profile was removed. For the native offline OpenAI-compatible BYOK adapter,\nchat and analysis with it also passed with a distinct `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID` such as\n`rea-gpt-4.1`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_MODEL=gpt-4.1`, and that distinct ID selected\nthrough `copilot --model rea-gpt-4.1`. The local fixture requested\n`COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS=1000000`; configure the limit supported by\nyour backend. This keeps every full schema and the actual wire model intact.\nIt does not establish the effective client budget or fix the built-in-ID path.\nThe compact input schemas passed native chat and analysis with the complete\ntool inventory on Linux using a loopback model fixture. Compact advertisements\ncan reduce nested schema constraints; REA still validates complete canonical\ninputs. Live model API acceptance and\nWindows remain unverified; see [native client verification](../development/testing.md).\n\n## Claude Desktop\n\nSetup registers `mcpServers.rea` in `claude_desktop_config.json`: under\n`~/Library/Application Support/Claude` on macOS, under\n`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Claude` (default `~/.config/Claude`) on Linux, and on Windows\nin the file the installed app reads:\n\n- Without Claude Desktop's MSIX package storage, setup uses\n `%APPDATA%\\Claude\\claude_desktop_config.json`.\n- The legacy MSIX storage layout (package family `Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc`, installed under\n `C:\\Program Files\\WindowsApps\\Claude__x64__pzs8sxrjxfjjc`)\n virtualizes AppData writes. Once it has saved its configuration, it reads\n the package-private copy\n `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Packages\\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc\\LocalCache\\Roaming\\Claude\\claude_desktop_config.json`\n and ignores the `%APPDATA%` file. Setup, doctor and uninstall use that\n private copy when it exists. Before the package has saved one, they use the\n `%APPDATA%` file it still reads; with neither file, setup creates the\n private copy.\n- If `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Claude-Data\\claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc` exists, setup, doctor\n and uninstall report an unresolved location. Migrated MSIX installations\n have been observed reading `claude_desktop_config.json` in this directory.\n Quit Claude Desktop and verify its active configuration before registering\n manually. See [#8968](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/8968).\n- If `%LOCALAPPDATA%\\Packages` holds a `Claude_` package from\n another publisher, an `AnthropicPBC.Claude_` package, or cannot\n be read, REA cannot establish which file Claude\n Desktop reads. Setup, doctor and uninstall report that instead of falling\n back to `%APPDATA%`. Doctor then reports `claude_desktop` as invalid, and\n uninstall stops before removing anything for any client.\n The reported `AnthropicPBC.Claude_fnn82j28hfe8t` build can use the `Claude-3p`\n deployment directory. REA recognizes that package as an unresolved location;\n it does not assume that it reads the legacy AppData file or automatically\n register in `Claude-3p`. See [#4432](https://github.com/morluto/rea/issues/4432)\n for the reported build and manual registration evidence.\n\nQuit Claude Desktop fully before approving setup; closing its window is not\nenough. A running Claude Desktop can rewrite its configuration from memory and\ndrop the registration. This was observed with the Windows MSIX build. Start\nClaude Desktop again after setup. If the package saves its private copy after\nsetup planned to write the `%APPDATA%` file, setup makes no change and asks you\nto rerun it.\n\nA process that the MSIX app started, such as a terminal in Claude Desktop's\nCode tab, sees the package's private files at their `%APPDATA%` paths even\nthough it reports no package identity. Setup compares one of those files at\nboth paths: first one from the package's private `Claude` folder, and when\nthat folder has none (some installations keep writing the real\n`%APPDATA%\\Claude`), one from the package's other private roaming folders,\nwhich the package redirects in the same way. When it finds that redirected\nview, the app is running, so setup and uninstall refuse to change Claude\nDesktop's configuration; rerun them from a terminal that Claude Desktop did not\nstart. If the package keeps no private roaming file at all, setup and\nuninstall cannot rule that out and also refuse. With Claude Desktop fully\nquit, add REA's entry by hand to the file setup names, which is the one the\napp reads, or remove it from both the private copy and the `%APPDATA%` file.\nDoctor reads the same file from either kind of process.\n\nThe same process also writes everything under `%APPDATA%` and\n`%LOCALAPPDATA%` into the package's private storage, where other apps never\nread it. From that redirected view, setup and uninstall refuse to change other\nclients' files there (VS Code, Trae, Devin and Hermes) and skill directories\nthere. `npm install -g` run from such a process installs into the package's\n`LocalCache\\Roaming\\npm`, which other processes cannot see at the `%APPDATA%`\npath. Setup refuses to register a launcher stored in any MSIX package's\nprivate storage. Install REA from an ordinary terminal and rerun setup there.\n\nUninstall removes REA's entry from both the private copy and the `%APPDATA%`\nfile, including registrations that earlier releases wrote to `%APPDATA%`.\n\nREA recognizes only the MSIX package.
